mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS) exceeding 2% coincident with a GDP contraction (GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY change < -2% AND GDPC1 YoY change < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both RSAFS YoY < -2% and GDPC1 YoY < 0%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of three consecutive months with UNRATE > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) below 97 for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which compresses earnings and capital expenditure, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO < 97 for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in CPIAUCSL below 2.0% while FEDFUNDS remains above 4.0% for two months signals a disinflationary environment with restrictive policy, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.0% AND FEDFUNDS > 4.0% for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL < 2.0% and FEDFUNDS > 4.0% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) above 5% for two consecutive months signals a robust housing recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month +5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST increases by more than 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in both PAYEMS and UNRATE by at least 0.3 percentage points indicates robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month +0.3% AND UNRATE > previous month +0.3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and UNRATE increase by at least 0.3% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent quarterly increase in GDP (GDPC1) above 2.5% for two consecutive quarters signals a strong demand-driven economic expansion, which supports higher corporate profits and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > previous quarter +2.5% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 increases by more than 2.5% for two consecutive quarters.
